Heard Sri. D.V. Pattar, learned counsel for the petitioner and Smt. Kirtilata R. Patil, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent No.1.
2.

The petitioner is before this Court seeking regular bail in crime No.297/2022 of respondent Police Station, for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 376 of IPC and Section 6 of the POCSO Act,
2012.

Brief facts of the case are:
3.
It is the case of the prosecution that the father of the victim has lodged a complaint stating that on 08.11.2022 at about 2.30 a.m., her minor daughter went to attend the nature call.
However, she did not come to the house.
After thorough search, as he could not get the information about his daughter, the complainant lodged a complaint before the jurisdictional police on 12.11.2022 around 8.00 p.m.
The jurisdictional police after registering the case in crime No.297/2022, conducted the investigation.
During the investigation, the fact of the case NC: 2024:KHC-D:9734 has been unfolded in such a way that the victim had discontinued her studies when she was studying at I PUC.
Thereafter, she left the school and stayed in the house and also assisting in agricultural work of their parents.
The petitioner herein had approached her when she was working in her land and also instigated her that he would marry her.

4. On 27.01.2022 at about 12.00 noon when the victim and the petitioner were standing near the Bakery and talking with each other, it was seen by the friend of her brother and it was informed to the brother of the victim.
The brother of the victim advised her not to proceed with the petitioner.
Till 06.11.2022 at about 10.30 a.m., they were not talking with each other.
However, on the same day, the petitioner insisted her to elope from the house and also assured her that he would marry her.
5. Believing his version, on 07.11.2022, she went out of the house along with the petitioner and stayed at different places.
Thereafter, they came back to NC: 2024:KHC-D:9734 Siddharoodha Math, Hubballi and there the petitioner is stated to have committed sexual assault against the minor.

Thereafter, on 20.11.2022 at about 11.00 a.m. when they went near Hubballi Railway station,
they were apprehended by the jurisdictional police.
The petitioner has been in judicial custody since 20.11.2022.
The jurisdictional police after conducting the investigation, submitted the charge sheet.
6. It is the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner is innocent of the alleged offence and he was not aware about the actual age of the victim.

As per the statement of the Sri Santosh Kumar vs State Of Karnataka on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129113373/
2 victim as on the date of the alleged incident, she was 17 years 9 months.

entities.text: Sri Santosh Kumar vs State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In fact, she informed the petitioner that she had completed 18 years and voluntarily went along with him at odd hours from her house and visited various places.
Thereafter, they returned to Hubballi and they have been apprehended near the Hubballi Railway station.

It is further submitted that the petitioner is ready to marry her, soon after he coming out of the judicial custody and he is permanent resident of Halebandiharlapur and he is the earning member of the family and he will abide the conditions imposed by this Court in the event of his release on bail.

8. Per contra, learned HCGP vehemently opposed the bail application and submitted that the petitioner has committed heinous offence against the minor girl and he has committed sexual assault by inducing her in one or the other pretext which in unpardonable.
9.
It is further submitted that now a days, the incident of such nature are being committed by the youths and adolescence in the name of marriage which needs to be regulated by the Courts.
If the petitioner is enlarged on bail, wrong message would be given to the society at large and also other youths would be awared about the consequences.

Therefore, it is not appropriate to grant him NC:
2024:KHC-D:9734 bail.
Making such submission, learned HCGP prays to dismiss the petition.

10. Having heard the learned counsel for respective parties and also perused the averments of the charge sheet, it appears from the record that both the victim and the petitioner were loving each other and in fact, they decided to marry each other.
Since, there is strong objection by the family of the victim as she had not completed age of majority, both the victim and the petitioner decided to elope from their respective houses for marriage.
However, they have been apprehended by the jurisdictional police.
As per the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner, the age of the victim has been misguided to the petitioner and the petitioner went along with her believing her version.
However, he learnt that she was minor only after he has been apprehended by the jurisdictional police.

The said fact appears to be true for the reason that the age of the NC:
2024:KHC-D:9734 victim as on the date of alleged incident was 17 years and 9 months.
11. On perusal of the entire records, no birth certificate is produced to determine the age of the victim.
Therefore, it is appropriate to grant him bail by imposing suitable conditions.

12. Hence, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition is allowed.

The petitioner is ordered to be enlarged on bail in Crime No.297/2022 of respondent Police Station, on executing a personal bond for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One lakh only) with one surety for the likesum to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional police and also the Trial Court, subject to the following conditions:-
